summary: Weekly POC sync focused on cost/unit economics. transcript:
[00:00] Marco Diaz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check - can you hear me? 
[00:05] Daniel Kim: Yep hear you Marco. 
[00:10] Marco Diaz: Cool. So agenda today - cost/unit review from the benchmark we ran last week, dig into caching and batching trade offs, and agree on next steps. Priya, you want to kick off with the numbers? 
[00:22] Priya Kapoor: Sure - I'll share screen (link: https://redwood.app/spreadsheets/poc-cost-model) - ok uh the headline, on the quantized 4-bit run we saw about 18,000 tokens per second baseline on the m60-equivalent nodes at the 16k prompt profile. That maps to roughly 0.0032 USD per 1k tokens when fully un-cached. 
[00:45] Ruth Alvarez: Sorry did you say 18k tokens per second or 1.8k? 
[00:49] Priya Kapoor: 18k, sorry that was mmmm quick phrasing - it's eighteen thousand tokens per second aggregated across the GPU pool under our test concurrency (we had 8 concurrent streams). 
[01:05] Samir Patel: That cost number seems low vs our expectations, can you walk through the cost calc? What assumptions on spot vs reserved and network egress? 
[01:15] Priya Kapoor: Yeah so the spreadsheet has three columns - hosted price (on-demand GPU), dedicated reserved (35% discount), and private on-prem (unit cost we estimated). The 0.0032 USD per 1k is for on-demand with our current throughput. If we apply 35% commit the unit drops to ~0.0021. We also added an estimated 0.0001 for network egress. 
[01:35] Marco Diaz: Important to note that's without caching - when we add prefix/KV caching the effective tokens/second per dollar improves a lot. Priya, show the cached run. 
[01:45] Priya Kapoor: For the cached experiment we simulated 70% prefix reuse and observed effective tokens/sec per dollar jump to equivalent of 55k tokens/sec - because repeat prefixes skip big decoder work. That drove the unit down to about 0.0011 USD per 1k. 
[02:05] Daniel Kim: The 70% is simulated; is that from our traffic? 
[02:10] Priya Kapoor: We used your sample traces you shared last week, extrapolated prefix overlap - looks like median reuse ~65% and top 20% sessions ~90% reuse. We can run a real KV-cache-enabled run next. 
[02:25] Samir Patel: Curious about latency impact when you increase batching to drive cost down - p50 is fine but p99 is what our customers see, any numbers there? 
[02:35] Priya Kapoor: Good call. In the 8-concurrency baseline batch size was small and p99 was ~240ms. When we increased batching aggressively to maximize tokens/sec the p99 jumped to ~680ms for the worst quantiles. With smart batching (deadline-based) we can control p99 to around 350-400ms and still capture ~70% of batching efficiency. 
[02:58] Marco Diaz: So tradeoff is cost vs tail latency - quantaco cares about interactive use-cases where p99 under 500ms is desirable. 
[03:10] Ruth Alvarez: Exactly, we can't sacrifice UX for cost. If we get 30-40% cost reduction with p99 staying under 450ms that'd be attractive. 
[03:20] Priya Kapoor: Another lever is model quantization and kernel selection - the 4-bit run gives big throughput wins but some small quality delta. We ran A/B evals on the prompt set and saw answer score drop of ~1.5% in our scoring. Might be acceptable but we'll measure on production prompts. 
[03:42] Daniel Kim: About caching - what about cache warming and memory footprint? Our longer prefixes are ~12k tokens, caching KV for many different prefixes could blow memory. 
[03:52] Priya Kapoor: Agreed. Our runtime supports partial/KV eviction policies, and we can page cold prefixes to SSD. For the tests we used a hot-key policy and saw memory growth contained - with 90% reuse it's fine. We'll need Samir's production prefix hist to model memory requirements precisely. 
[04:10] Samir Patel: I'll pull the histogram and share. Also, for Dedicated capacity we're interested in deterministic p99 - what sizing do you recommend? 
[04:20] Marco Diaz: For deterministic p99 at your projected qps and 90% prefix reuse, we suggest starting with a 3-GPU pool (M60-equivalent) with headroom for bursts; the spreadsheet has a sizing tab. We'll follow up with a dedicated sizing call. 
[04:35] Ruth Alvarez: Can you also include a scenario with only 50% prefix reuse? We want conservative forecasts for finance. 
[04:42] Priya Kapoor: Yep - the sheet has 50/70/90% tabs, I'll make sure the summary slide includes the 50% scenario. 
[04:50] Marco Diaz: Quick question on security - in private deployment we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs retention for 7 years. Any blockers? 
[04:58] Priya Kapoor: We support KMS integrations and can push audit logs to your ELK/Splunk. Retention policies are configurable; for on-prem some customers handle the archive with object storage. We'll share our security docs. 
[05:12] Daniel Kim: Great. A few clarifying Qs from the bench - can you run the cached test with our exact model checkpoints and full request trace? 
[05:20] Priya Kapoor: Yes we can; I'll need the trace and a pointer to the checkpoint (or we can pull from your registry). That will give the most representative numbers. 
[05:30] Marco Diaz: Ok let's align on next steps - recap with owners. 
[05:34] Marco Diaz: Marco - send cost spreadsheet and summarizing slides by Friday 2026-05-08. 
[05:40] Priya Kapoor: Priya - run the cached 90% prefix run and the 2 batching variants, upload logs by 2026-05-10. 
[05:47] Samir Patel: Samir - send prefix histogram + request distribution by 2026-05-09 and confirm whether we can provide test VPC creds for the run. 
[05:57] Ruth Alvarez: I'll confirm internal stakeholders for dedicated sizing and get back by 2026-05-11. 
[06:05] Marco Diaz: Thanks everyone. We'll schedule the dedicated sizing call for the following week once we have the hist and logs. 
[06:12] Daniel Kim: Thanks all. 
[06:15] [call ends]
